title: The pro-étale direct image for all finite-Tor objects
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$, and the algebraically closed field
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes with
$\dim X\leq d$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-modules on the small pro-étale site with
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, both notions being the intrinsic ones of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $Rf_*K$ is bounded
constructible on $Y_{\Proet}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. That is, clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at
the finite coefficient stage $A$ for *every* object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$, with no restriction to the objects of étale
origin.

proof.text: Use the finite-ring constructible-derived-origin essential-image criterion with B = Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n. Finiteness follows from hn. The finite support of the intrinsic cohomology supplies explicit lower and upper integer bounds, so the criterion supplies a bounded constructible etale complex K' and an isomorphism from the specified intrinsic derived comparison of K' to K. This is the derived etale-origin step required by the unit, directly in the constant-ring coefficient presentation.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: every bounded constructible complex is of etale origin; Stacks Tags 09AK and 09AL (proetale.tex, lemma-compare-constructible and lemma-compare-constructible-derived).

proof.text: The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ and $Y$, since both are schemes over the characteristic-$p$ field $k$ and $\ell\ne p$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] applies to $K$, $K'$ and $e$: its required bounded-below hypothesis on $K'$ was checked in step 1. It gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for $K'$ on the etale site, with the same constant coefficient ring $A$.

Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] to $f$ and $K'$. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, separated finite-type morphism $f$, source dimension bound $\dim X\le d$, bounded constructibility from step 1, and Tor interval from step 2. Thus $L:=Rf_{\Et,*}K'$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. No properness or separatedness of the structure morphism of $X$ is added. Convert the two equivalent finite-ring etale constructibility predicates with the existing constructible-etale-module-sheaf comparison theorem. The bundled Over objects supply the structure-map and IsOver instances for the current directImageCTFNonproper interface.

proof.text: Apply isIso_comparisonDirectImagePlus to the bounded-below complex K' and f. Use rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility and mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility on both sites to obtain the isomorphism in the unbounded derived categories. Factor the intrinsic comparison into fixed-coefficient inverse image followed by intrinsic realization using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. The existing section-normalized sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison commutes realization past direct image. Compose with derived direct image of the origin isomorphism to identify the comparison image of L = Rf_Et,* K' with the original intrinsic direct image Rf_Proet,* K.

source.place: Proof, displayed direct-image comparison; Stacks Tag 09A6 (proetale.tex, lemma-morphism-comparison), in the comparison section Tag 099R cited by the dependency.

proof.text: Apply finiteCoefficient_comparison_preserves_torAmplitude to L and [a,b+2d]. Transport finite cohomological support through the homology isomorphisms. Transport each intrinsic constructible homology sheaf by proEtaleModuleRestriction_constructible_iff and isConstructible_of_iso. For the Tor predicate, every representative isomorphic to the original direct image is also isomorphic to the comparison image by composition; apply the comparison-image Tor hypothesis to exactly that representative, resolution and test module. This proves both conclusions for the arbitrary intrinsic K.
